picks.name: @react-three/drei
picks.licenseEvidence: LICENSE file at pmndrs/drei/blob/master/LICENSE states 'MIT License'
picks.gives: Ready-made R3F helpers: Float (idle bob/tilt), Sparkles, MeshDistortMaterial, Trail, useCursor — covers orb idle motion and holo card hover in a few props
picks.risk: Pulls in @react-three/fiber; verify version compat with three 0.186.x before pinning

picks.name: three.quarks
picks.licenseEvidence: LICENSE file (root) — MIT License, Copyright (c) 2019 Forrest Sun
picks.gives: Full particle/VFX engine for three.js: emitters, curves, sprite-batch particles — good for orb idle glow/ambient particles and holo card shimmer
picks.where: https://github.com/Alchemist0823/three.quarks (examples/ folder, live demos linked from README)
picks.risk: No GitHub Releases page — pin an exact npm version, not a branch/tag, to avoid drift

picks.name: react-spring / @react-spring/three
picks.licenseEvidence: LICENSE file at pmndrs/react-spring/blob/main/LICENSE — MIT, Copyright (c) 2018-present Paul Henschel and contributors
picks.gives: Spring-physics hooks (useSpring, animated) with a three.js-native binding for hover/idle scale, rotation, emissive intensity on orb/cards
picks.risk: Last tagged release mid-2024 — check open issues for React 19/three 0.186 compat before pinning

picks.name: Motion (formerly Framer Motion)
picks.licenseEvidence: LICENSE.md at motiondivision/motion — 'The MIT License (MIT)', Copyright (c) 2024 Motion B.V.
picks.gives: DOM/CSS animation engine (springs, gestures, layout) — best for HTML overlay UI on holo cards (hover tilt, glow) composited over the WebGL canvas, not for in-scene 3D objects
picks.risk: No native three.js/WebGL binding — only animates DOM/CSS, so it's for card chrome, not the orb mesh itself

picks.name: simplex-noise
picks.licenseEvidence: LICENSE file — MIT, Copyright (c) 2018 Jonas Wagner
picks.gives: Dependency-free simplex noise generator (~2KB min+gzip per README) for driving organic idle bob/rotation on the orb in the render loop
picks.risk: CPU-side only; for shader-driven noise use webgl-noise instead

picks.name: webgl-noise (Ashima Arts)
picks.licenseEvidence: README states 'Source code for the noise functions is released under the conditions of the MIT license. See the file LICENSE for details.'
picks.gives: Classic GLSL noise (Perlin/simplex) snippets to paste into custom ShaderMaterial for idle shimmer on orb/holo card surfaces
picks.risk: Unmaintained/archival — copy the specific .glsl function you need rather than depending on the repo

picks.name: mattdesl/eases
picks.gives: Small grab-bag of Penner easing equations (JS + glsl-easings derived) as a lightweight easing pack for tweening idle/hover motion
picks.risk: Low recent activity — fine since it's a frozen math utility, but confirm it still installs cleanly

rejected.name: LottieFiles free library
rejected.licenseEvidence: lottiefiles.com/page/license: free, commercial use allowed, no attribution required, modifications become derivatives under same license, may not be scraped/recompiled into a competing library
rejected.gives: Free Lottie JSON animations usable for splash/title choreography accents if a 2D overlay layer is added later
rejected.risk: Per-file license, not a code dependency — any file actually pulled needs a CREDITS.md line (name, URL, license, date) before shipping
rejected.reason: license not allowed: Lottie Simple License (custom, not OSI)
rejected.rejectedBy: license-gate: license not allowed: Lottie Simple License (custom, not OSI)

rejected.name: LYGIA shader library
rejected.reason: Dual-licensed under Prosperity License + Patron License — non-commercial free only, requires paid license for commercial use, fails MIT/Apache-2.0/CC0 filter

rejected.name: Shadertoy snippets
rejected.reason: Per-shader licensing, most default to CC BY-NC-SA (non-commercial) with no uniform terms — too risky to copy into a commercial desktop app without per-shader verification

top: @react-three/drei — MIT, actively released (v10.7.9, Sep 2026), gives Float/Sparkles/Trail out of the box for orb+card idle motion
three.quarks — MIT particle VFX engine purpose-built for three.js, best fit for orb ambient particles and holo shimmer
react-spring/@react-spring/three — MIT spring-physics hooks with a native R3F binding for smooth hover transitions on meshes
